gitCommit.subject: feat(sorting): Epic P — batched decision pipeline (no tap waits on the database) (#307)
gitCommit.body:
feat(sorting): Epic P — batched decision pipeline (no tap waits on the database) (#307)

* docs(specs): sort-unification parent spec (rev 3) + Epic P batched-decisions mechanism spec

Parent spec adversarially reviewed (5 personas) with findings folded; rev 3 folds
the user's timer-default decision (timed 2m default, 'No timer' first-class).
Epic P spec pending its own adversarial review.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(specs): fold Epic P adversarial review (34 findings → 20 edits) + timer-default decision

Epic P spec rev 2: ItemId schema fix (block — bare-ULID regex would have 400'd
every real batch), ON CONFLICT duplicate handling (25P02 fix), DB now() as
ordering authority, disposition-409 split, What-moved recap from merged
client+server data, selectTriageQueue defined, gate mount/timeout contract,
Web-Lock cross-tab single-flight, storage GC. Parent spec rev 3 + errata.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(plans): Epic P batched-decisions implementation plan (17 tasks + deferred e2e; ambiguities resolved)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(ordering): one shared (createdAt,id) comparator for both event consumers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(id): generateOrderedIdFactory — monotonic event ids preserving prefix+lowercase

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(batch): shared Zod batch schema (repo-format ids pinned) + stream-budget body reader

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(batch): POST /api/sessions/[id]/decisions/batch — gates, stream body cap, whole-batch validation

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(batch): semantic validation, idempotency, ON CONFLICT dedupe, recompute predicate, analytics

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(decisions): drop unreachable 23505 catch-and-re-read (advisory lock serializes; re-read would 25P02)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(queue): versioned curator-keyed pending/quarantine storage with GC + quota fallback

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(flusher): single-flight Web-Lock drain engine with ordered runs, backoff, and failure taxonomy

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(epicP): stage C review fixes

- ackId: write the NUL separator as the \u0000 escape instead of a raw
  0x00 byte so git treats decisionFlusher.ts as text (diffs/blame work);
  the runtime string is byte-identical.
- handleBatchFailure 400: drop the dead re-validation filter (everything
  sent passed BatchEntrySchema in the same lock iteration, so it always
  yielded []) and quarantine the sent chunk directly — the documented,
  tested behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(triage): selectTriageQueue — whole eligible remainder; selectTriageItem = first entry

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(triage): optimistic client round — queue advance, one round-end refresh, frozen recap merge

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(triage): undo-as-revisit — standing answer shown, latest-wins supersede, disposition gating

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(notices): one quiet person-side line for rejected/quarantined answers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(dispositions): Not mine / Not yet ride the decision queue — network leaves the tap path

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(compare): submit as idempotent batch-of-1 through the queue/flusher — never a bare fetch

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(recovery): PendingDecisionsGate — drain-then-reveal with bounded catch-up + storage GC

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(sessions): shared status-PATCH helper — non-blocking pause pre-flush, strict flush-then-complete

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(graphify): refresh committed graph for tasks 14-16

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(bench): 50 single POSTs vs 1x50 batch amortization benchmark + API docs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(architecture): decision 27 — batched decision pipeline (Epic P)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(graphify): refresh graph post doc-sync

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(screenshots): welcome beat-4 waits for the real h1 (drift from #304 walkthrough rebuild)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(e2e): batch-route decision waits + bring-back un-ends an exhausted round (Epic P)

Epic P moved compare and triage decisions onto the queue/flusher, so the
POST lands at …/decisions/batch, not …/decisions. Three e2e specs still
awaited the superseded single-decision route and timed out at 30s:

- compare.spec / sort-session.spec: point waitForResponse at the batch route.
- not-yet-defer.spec: a tap no longer emits a per-tap POST; advance on the UI
  (next card focuses or the deferred item resurfaces) and assert one batch
  flush after both taps. sort-session also arms the round-end RSC-refresh
  waiter before the tap so it doesn't race the next page.goto().

Also fixes a real product bug surfaced by the flow (TDD, 4 tests): "Bring back"
after a queue-exhausted round left the recap on screen — a dead-end escape.
TriageRound now un-ends a queue-exhausted round on restore while leaving a
timer-expired round ended (the time box is the boundary).

The not-mine-set-aside failure in CI was worker-restart collateral from the
compare timeout; it passes once the timeout is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016Ut8X3F3dNUGeJGAjPESvb

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(e2e): batch-route decision waits + bring-back un-ends an exhausted round (Epic P)

Epic P moved compare and triage decisions onto the queue/flusher, so the
POST lands at …/decisions/batch, not …/decisions. Three e2e specs still
awaited the superseded single-decision route and timed out at 30s:

- compare.spec / sort-session.spec: point waitForResponse at the batch route.
- not-yet-defer.spec: a tap no longer emits a per-tap POST; advance on the UI
  (next card focuses or the deferred item resurfaces) and assert one batch
  flush after both taps. sort-session also arms the round-end RSC-refresh
  waiter before the tap so it doesn't race the next page.goto().

Also fixes a real product bug surfaced by the flow (TDD, 4 tests): "Bring back"
after a queue-exhausted round left the recap on screen — a dead-end escape.
TriageRound now un-ends a queue-exhausted round on restore while leaving a
timer-expired round ended (the time box is the boundary).

The not-mine-set-aside failure in CI was worker-restart collateral from the
compare timeout; it passes once the timeout is gone.
